chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I think it is Isحاق ibn Ghaleb, who said:

When a man rises for prayer at night and supposes that dawn has broken, so he prays the Witr, then he looks and sees that night is still upon him, he said: 'He adds one rak'ah to the Witr, then he faces the night prayer, then he prays Witr after it.'

key_terms.الوَتْر: Witr, the odd-numbered prayer concluding the night prayer

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they pray Witr thinking dawn has broken, but then realize it is still night?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific scenario of *shakk* (doubt) regarding the onset of Fajr after completing Witr, prescribing a corrective sequence of adding one rak'ah to the Witr, performing the remaining night prayer, and concluding with a new Witr. This method ensures the validity of the night prayer while maintaining the distinct status of Witr as the final prayer of the night, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precision in ritual structure. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the obligatory nature of the night prayer and the recommended (mustahabb) yet distinct nature of Witr.
